correctness.rationale: For probability-normalized sphere measure, squared coordinates are Dirichlet with all parameters 1/2 and the independent signs give an orthant factor 2^-n. On the full-sphere orthonormal traceless diagonal and off-diagonal bases, the rescaled diagonal block is identity. For edge pairs the moments give 1, s, s² for equal, adjacent and disjoint pairs, hence B=(1−s)²I+s(1−s)R*R+s²J with unsigned incidence R. In the mixed moment the terms with a diagonal index on the edge have twice the generic moment; after summing the generic part against the traceless coefficients, the cross block is (s/√2)R*. Since RR*=(n−2)I+J_n, constants give T and ker R gives e with the stated dimension (zero at n=3). On the sum-zero image normalization of R* supplies √(n−2), giving n−1 identical 2-by-2 blocks with entries 1,b,b,a. The dimensions exhaust the complex harmonic space. Both T−1 and T−a exceed b; the shifted determinant at e is (n−2)s²(2s²−6s+3)/2<0 at s=2/π. Thus the top mode is unique up to scalar, and the spectral gap controls the orthogonal component sharply, with equality on any second-branch vector. The expansion T=(s²/2)n²+O(n), a=ns(1−s)+O(1), b=O(√n), gives r_+=ns(1−s)+O(1) from the quadratic eigenvalue formula for large n. It yields both stated limits, including s/[2(1−s)]=1/(π−2) for the top-to-second coefficient.
residual_risks: The archived finite numerical and symbolic tests were inspected, not run; the all-dimensional conclusion rests on the normalized moment, incidence and spectral arguments.
